A bank manager quit
at forty. Coffee followed.
slides.subline: Terarosa Coffee Factory, Gangneung — the 2002 roastery-cafe credited with turning a seaside city into Korea's coffee destination

slides.title:
The city followed
the cafe, not the other way round.
slides.body:
Gangneung is now shorthand for coffee in Korea, and the sequence matters: the roastery came first. Kim Yong-deok opened Terarosa here in 2002 after twenty-one years as a bank branch manager, in a farming district well outside the city centre — not on the beachfront where the coffee crowds later gathered.

The pull worked in reverse. Enthusiasts drove out to the factory, Gangneung's coffee reputation grew around them, and the city launched its Coffee Festival in 2009 — an event The Asia Business Daily reports now draws around 200,000 visitors a year.

The founder is no longer part of it. That paper reported in April 2026 that Kim had sold his entire remaining 24.2% stake in operator Haksan to the private equity firm UCK Partners, which now holds 74.3% of a chain of 34 directly managed stores. What is left at Hyeoncheon-gil is the original building — worth knowing before you make the drive.

items.d: Korean listings give the cafe as no. 7 and Terarosa's own site registers the company at no. 25 on the same road; it sits beside the Namgangneung IC exit

items.t: Hours differ by source — confirm first
items.d: The tourism listing says 09:00-21:00 for coffee and bakery; Korean listings show earlier closes on weekdays. Phone 033-648-2760

items.t: It is a drive, not a walk from the station
items.d: The site is out in a rural district rather than on Anmok Beach's coffee street, so plan transport rather than wandering over

caption:
A bank branch manager quit at forty, went home to Gangneung, and put a coffee roaster inside the cafe.

Terarosa Coffee Factory has stood in Gujeong-myeon since 2002 — red brick, a working roastery, bakery and garden — and Gangneung has been known as Korea's coffee city since.

Hours differ by listing, so check before the drive.
